candidate_relations.reason: The clinical picture—chronic non-pitting periorbital edema in a young adult without acne/rosacea, negative patch and TB tests, biopsy showing ectatic vessels/lymphatics with sparse lymphocytic infiltrate—fits solid persistent facial edema (Morbihan disease). Lymphangioma is a congenital vascular malformation that would typically present earlier in life, show a discrete mass lesion on imaging, and have a different histopathological pattern (multiloculated cystic lymphatic channels). While both involve lymphatic structures, lymphangioma asserts an incompatible etiology and diagnostic category relative to the benchmark.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Lymphangioma is a congenital/hamartomatous vascular malformation; solid persistent facial edema (Morbihan disease) is a chronic lymphedematous condition of the face, distinct in etiology, scope, and diagnostic category

case_quality_flags: Biopsy findings of ectatic blood vessels and lymphatics with sparse lymphocytic infiltrate are classic for solid persistent facial edema (Morbihan disease); absence of acne/rosacea history is atypical but documented in the literature
